question: Why cannot apprehending one thing yield apprehension of another lacking its own form?
premises: Apprehension depends on the nature of the object.
One thing cannot substitute for another's nature.
Grasping something else does not constitute grasping the target.
inference: Perception of one thing cannot establish perception of another.
plain_english: When something does not have its own proper form, apprehending another thing does not amount to apprehending it.
